logline: A woman who remembers every one of her past nineteen lives tracks down the man she loved and lost in a previous incarnation, only to find grief and recognition are not the same thing.

seasons.review_body: See You in My 19th Life aired on tvN from June to July 2023 and streamed internationally via Netflix, adapting a popular webtoon of the same name. The premise - a woman named Ban Ji-eum retains full memories of 18 previous lives and devotes her 19th to reconnecting with Moon Seo-ha, a man she loved before a tragic accident ended her last incarnation - is generous in its emotional architecture if sometimes strained in its internal logic. Shin Hye-sun carries the series on sustained conviction, selling the eerie dissonance of adult knowledge packaged in a young body. The tvN nationwide average of 4.664% sustained across 12 episodes indicates consistent viewership rather than a breakout hit. Rotten Tomatoes aggregated no formal critic consensus, but the 82% audience score and a 7.7 IMDb rating point to a drama that rewards fans of webtoon-adjacent supernatural romance even as its structural quirks accumulate.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere front-loads the reincarnation concept with admirable clarity - Ji-eum's perfect recall is framed as both gift and wound, and Shin Hye-sun's physicality sells the uncanny before a single plot point lands.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Ji-eum recognises Seo-ha across a lobby, and the camera holds long enough on her face to convey nineteen lifetimes of longing in a single beat.
